items.title: Anthropic becomes one of world's most valuable public companies in stock market debut
items.description: Anthropic is the first purely AI company to be publicly listed, creating a test for the entire industry.

items.title: 'I tell my son it's just fireworks': People inside besieged Yemeni city speak to BBC
items.description: Orla Guerin speaks to seven people trapped in Taiz by the Houthis who reveal what life is like under siege.

items.title: Myanmar committed genocide against Rohingya minority, top UN court rules
items.description: The unprecedented International Court of Justice verdict concerns a 2017 military crackdown that killed thousands.

items.title: Europe ready for talks with Russia on ending war in Ukraine, leaders say
items.description: European allies of Ukraine say they have a "united" negotiating position at a summit in Berlin.

items.title: Trump, Putin and Xi release 'peace declaration' after historic meeting
items.description: While the presidents have previously met for one-on-one meetings, this is their first trilateral discussion.

items.title: California targets Nvidia in China AI chip probe
items.description: The probe by California, where the AI chipmaker has its global headquarters, follows former CEO Jensen Huang's departure.

items.title: Fiona the hippo dies after swallowing a hat at Cincinnati Zoo
items.description: Fiona, who became an internet star after her premature birth in 2017, "fought until she couldn’t anymore", the zoo says.

items.title: Judge finds Thomas Markle mentally fit to stand trial on child abuse charges
items.description: Markle, who has denied possessing images of child sex abuse was deemed competent after an evaluation by a court-appointed psychiatrist.

items.title: Trump posthumously pardons US baseball legend Pete Rose
items.description: Rose, who died in 2024, was given a lifetime ban from the sport for betting on games but was reinstated last year.

items.title: Dozens missing after boat carrying migrants sinks off Senegal's coast
items.description: At least four bodies have been recovered from the boat which was reportedly carrying between 50 and 100 people.

items.title: Putin vows 'far more painful' response to Ukraine's strikes on Crimean Bridge
items.description: The bridge - a symbol of Russia's occupation of the Crimean Peninsula - suffered major damaged following a combined attack by Ukraine earlier this week.

items.title: Van Gogh painting sells for record $190.4m after row over its Nazi history
items.description: Châtaigniers en fleurs was painted in 1890 in the final two months of Vincent van Gogh's life.

items.title: Venezuela signs military deal with US less than a year after Maduro's removal
items.description: The US Secretary of Defence says Venezuela has "gone from our most aggressive regional threat to a compliant security partner".

items.title: Susan Smith denied parole again 32 years after drowning her two sons
items.description: At a hearing on the possibility of parole, Smith said she wished she could change the past, and her two children "did not deserve to die".

items.title: US consortium wins huge Kenya mining deal, beating Chinese rivals
items.description: The Mrima Hill site is estimated to hold deposits of critical minerals worth more than $60bn (£45bn).

items.title: Survivors of Uganda's deadly landslide seek justice at the UN
items.description: Survivors reject relocation plans they say ignore their safety, land rights and livelihoods.

items.title: Florida pastor found guilty over role in assassination of Haitian president
items.description: Christian Emmanuel Sanon is convicted of involvement in the plot that resulted in the killing of Jovenel Moïse.

items.title: Israeli military completes ground operation in Gaza beyond Yellow Line
items.description: Hamas condemned the incursion, which the Israeli military said was to dismantle a "terror tunnel", as a "flagrant" ceasefire violation.

items.title: Elon Musk says record $446m spending on US midterms was 'pretty foolish'
items.description: The multi-billionaire also said he was "not Maga", distancing himself from the political movement linked to Trump.

items.title: Inside the old gas pipeline where Ukraine is fighting an underground war with Russia
items.description: Watch: The BBC's Jonathan Beale joins Ukrainian forces taking the battle below ground and out of sight of Russian drones.
